key_insight: Photonic variational circuits are trainable when observable variance shrinks only polynomially with system size, but become impractical for high-order or probability-based observables that need exponentially many samples.
engineering_relevance: This provides a design rule for choosing measurements in near-term photonic quantum algorithms so gradients and loss changes can be estimated with feasible sampling costs.
method: Define trainability using the ratio of sample variance to circuit variance.
Analyze photon-number observables to separate polynomial-sample regimes from exponential-sample regimes.
Identify neural-network-based observables that can efficiently process measurement outcomes into useful polynomial observables.
evidence_signal: The paper combines analytic results with numerically observed polynomial decay of circuit variance to show that fixed-order photon-number polynomials scale with only polynomially many samples, while high-order polynomials and output probabilities typically do not.
watch_item: The practical benefit depends on choosing observables in the trainable regime; otherwise sampling costs can still grow exponentially and negate near-term advantages.
paper_title: The trainability of photonic quantum circuits
